title: Precision Probiotics to Modulate Autonomic and Vascular Function in Menopause
official: Precision Probiotics to Modulate Autonomic and Vascular Function in Menopause
summary:
This randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled pilot study will investigate the effects of an Akkermansia muciniphila-based probiotic supplement, Panthea Core, on autonomic and vascular function in postmenopausal women with hypertension.

Up to 60 participants aged 45 to 65 years will be enrolled to obtain approximately 40 evaluable datasets. Participants will be randomly assigned to receive Panthea Core or a matched placebo capsule daily for 12 weeks.

The study will evaluate safety, tolerability, menopausal symptoms, and changes in autonomic and vascular physiology. The primary mechanistic outcome is muscle sympathetic nerve activity (MSNA), measured using microneurography. Secondary physiological outcomes include heart rate variability, baroreflex sensitivity, endothelial function assessed by flow-mediated dilation, and blood pressure.

Additional assessments will include sleep, menopausal symptoms, mood, cognitive function, circulating metabolic markers, and gut microbiome composition. Participants will complete baseline and post-intervention assessments, with additional safety monitoring throughout supplementation and approximately one month after the intervention.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Female individuals, assigned female sex at birth, aged 45 to 65 years.
* Clinician-diagnosed hypertension, either controlled or uncontrolled.
* Postmenopausal status, defined as at least 12 months without menstruation or prior surgical removal of the ovaries.
* Willing and able to provide informed consent.

Exclusion Criteria:

* Nicotine/tobacco, probiotic, or antibiotic use within the previous six months.
* Body mass index of 40 kg/m² or greater.
* Use of hormonal contraceptives or systemic exogenous hormones.
* Diagnosis of diabetes.
* Respiratory disease other than well-controlled asthma.
* Severe neurological conditions, including traumatic brain injury or stroke.
* Existing endocrine abnormalities.
* History of chemotherapy.
* Surgery within the preceding six months.
* Autoimmune disorders.
* History of organ transplantation.
* Digestive disorders, including active or unstable gastrointestinal disease, major gastrointestinal surgery, or motility disorders.
* Immunosuppressive or glucocorticoid therapy.
* Chronic illnesses that preclude participation at the investigator's discretion.
* Intermittent fasting with unwillingness or inability to complete a four-week washout period before enrollment.
* Inability to speak, read, or understand English.
* Inability to provide informed consent.
